items.tradition: Chinese oracle-bone script; modern vector redraw based on cited Hanziyuan and Academia Sinica character images
items.caption: A modern redraw of 車 in Shang oracle-bone style. Early variants could spell out several parts of a vehicle; this drawing is an example of the script style, not a photograph of an oracle bone.
items.alt: Black vector drawing of an oracle-bone style form of 車 on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: Offers an early graphic example relevant to the pictographic vehicle analysis; the page gives specific source-image references and CC0/public-domain terms.
items.rights: CC0 / public-domain dedication stated on the Commons page.

items.tradition: Chinese bronze-inscription script; modern vector redraw keyed to the cited 同卣 inscription image
items.caption: A modern redraw of 車 in Western Zhou bronze-script style. The Commons description links this form to an image of the character on the mid-Western Zhou vessel 同卣.
items.alt: Black vector drawing of a Western Zhou bronze-script form of 車 on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: Adds a sourced intermediate form between oracle-bone and seal styles and identifies a particular mid-Western Zhou inscription image.
items.rights: CC0 / public-domain dedication stated on the Commons page.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script tradition; transmitted dictionary form, compiled c. 100 CE
items.tradition: Chinese seal script; modern vector redraw referencing Hanziyuan and Academia Sinica
items.caption: A modern redraw of the 車 form associated with the Shuowen seal-script tradition, showing a more regularized shape than the cited oracle-bone and bronze examples.
items.alt: Black vector drawing of 車 in seal-script style on a plain background.
items.selection_reason: Shows a later, regularized script style to accompany the older inscription-based forms; the page names its source image and reusable rights.
items.rights: Public-domain dedication stated on the Commons page.

limitations.text: The image candidates are modern vector redrawings rather than photos of ancient artifacts. The captions describe their cited script styles and provenance, not visual observations made in this research pass.

Direct SVG rendering failed in the web tool, though exact original-file URLs were obtained by following each Commons page’s Original file link. Download success remains to be checked by the acquisition harness.
